observations: Historical connected-player preparation checks body mass and terrain support and prepares inventory geometry for the applicable batch before projecting commands; unmatched loading players are skipped and multiple terrain authorities are rejected. Connected upstream admission, all command failure modes and actual scheduling remain open.

Historical item geometry separates unit mass from tactical quantity, prefers derived weapon or holder mass when present, and derives physical anchor offset for parametric weapons. Projected weapon geometry checks version, recipe, identity, hash and properties; holder projection uses assertions and expectations that rely on a separately validated strategic authority. Those prerequisites and failure reachability were not proven here.

Historical armor projection selects authored placement and coverage and expects catalog metadata to have been validated. Its later relationship to equipment topology and contacts requires a connected trace; separately recorded 95e findings do not establish this older snapshot as current.

Historical airborne dive projects camera-relative horizontal velocity while a grounded slide preserves velocity. Facing advances from posture, attack and configuration and transfers transition yaw into both transform and physics rotation. Referenced animation invariants, native scheduling and admitted numeric boundaries remain open.

Historical terrain digest helper validates hexadecimal input through SourcePackageDigest but returns raw hex strings from SHA-256 operations. All source tests were read, not run; no product build, test, simulation or runtime probe ran.
remaining: Trace strategic producer validation and tactical consumers of weapon and holder identity, mass, armor and attachment frames; connect spawn transaction and motion scheduling; trace terrain package digest propagation. Reconcile historical aliases and independently assess every lens.
